references.text: Moses calls heaven and earth as witnesses against Israel when they choose between life and death, blessing and curse, just as Joshua calls the people to be witnesses against themselves.
A song shall serve as a witness against the children of Israel, similar to how the people's own words become a witness against them in Joshua.
Joshua's call to the people to choose whom they will serve, which is the background for their declaration that they have chosen the Lord.
The stone that Joshua sets up shall be a witness, complementing the people's role as witnesses against themselves.
Job calls upon a witness in heaven, highlighting the theme of witnesses in a covenant context.
Israel is called to be witnesses for the Lord, a theme that reflects the people's role as witnesses in Joshua.
The Lord calls the nations as witnesses against them, parallel to how Israel are witnesses against themselves.
Jesus says that the servant will be judged by his own words, similar to how Israel's own words become a witness against them.
